record.original_question: For the cubic family x' = ax + by, y' = cx^3 + dx^2 y + ex y^2 + fy^3, determine whether 2 is the maximum possible number of limit cycles; and for the more concrete equation x' = y, y' = -x^3 + dx^2 y + y^3, determine whether the limit cycle, when it exists, is unique and give a simple proof of that fact if it is true.

evidence.quote: Problem 3. (i) Consider the cubic family (...) Is 2 its maximum number of limit cycles? (ii) Give a simple proof, if it is true, of the uniqueness of the limit cycle for equation (...)

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the family of planar cubic homogeneous-nonlinearity differential systems
$$\dot x = a x + b y, \qquad \dot y = c x^3 + d x^2 y + e x y^2 + f y^3,$$
with real parameters $a,b,c,d,e,f \in \mathbb{R}$, where a limit cycle is an isolated periodic orbit in the phase plane.

(i) Determine whether the maximum number of limit cycles that this family can possess (over all admissible parameter values) is exactly $2$. That is, prove that every system in this family has at most two limit cycles, or exhibit a parameter choice producing three or more limit cycles.

(ii) For the one-parameter subfamily
$$\dot x = y, \qquad \dot y = -x^3 + d x^2 y + y^3, \qquad d \in \mathbb{R},$$
decide whether, whenever a limit cycle exists, it is unique, and provide a simple proof of this uniqueness if it holds.
artifact.category_tag: Limit cycles of polynomial planar vector fields
artifact.status_search_result: Web searches did not surface a definitive resolution of either part: no source confirms that 2 is the sharp maximum number of limit cycles for the cubic family $\dot x=ax+by,\ \dot y=cx^3+dx^2y+exy^2+fy^3$, nor a published simple uniqueness proof for the limit cycle of $\dot x=y,\ \dot y=-x^3+dx^2y+y^3$. The problem appears to remain open as posed.

status_evidence.title: Limit cycles of cubic polynomial vector fields via the averaging theory
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses bounds on numbers of limit cycles bifurcating in cubic polynomial perturbations; does not establish a sharp bound of 2 for the specified family.
status_evidence.claim: No definitive bound of 2 limit cycles is established for this cubic family in the literature retrieved.

status_evidence.title: On the Uniqueness of Limit Cycles in a Generalized Liénard System
status_evidence.snippet: General uniqueness criteria for generalized Liénard systems are surveyed, but not applied specifically to $\dot x=y, \dot y=-x^3+dx^2y+y^3$.
status_evidence.claim: No simple uniqueness proof for the specific cubic equation is reported.
